svg.text: Complete connection picture • all ESP32 pin boxes below refer to the SAME board.
Unplug USB before moving wires. Follow pin names and hole labels, not wire colour alone.
1 EXTERNAL LED — controlled by D2 / GPIO 2
Exact holes: D2 → A6 • resistor E6–E10 • LED + A10 / − A13 • GND → B13
A–E holes in the SAME numbered row connect internally. Different rows are separate.
The LED legs must be in different rows. The resistor can face either way.
D4 → B19 • GND → B22. Keep the buzzer legs in DIFFERENT rows.
Use the + mark on the buzzer to identify its positive leg.
Wire its three labelled pins directly.
Match the labels on YOUR PIR.
check its printed labels before wiring.
Do not connect PIR VCC to D5.
FIND THE PINS ON YOUR ESP32
Front / component side • USB at the TOP
Use printed labels, not counted pin positions.
1. Unplug USB and rebuild ONE external LED circuit first.
2. Add the buzzer in rows 19 and 22, then wire the PIR.
3. Female jumper end → ESP32 pin. Male end → breadboard hole.
4. Plug USB in; close Arduino Serial Monitor; connect the app.
5. In Sensors & lights, press Full brightness to check the LED.
6. Switch Buzzer on and press Run test to check both.
WHY THE ESP32 LIGHTS UP BUT THE EXTERNAL LED DOES NOT
Your sketch drives D2. Onboard light activity does not verify the external circuit.
Check LED polarity, the series resistor, hole numbers, and the GND connection.
Do not connect a bare LED directly to D2 or 3V3. Keep the series resistor.
